about.label: About
about.title: From raw documents and data to *reliable AI*
paragraphs: I'm a Machine Learning Engineer with an MSc in Computer Science & Engineering from Politecnico di Milano (110/110 cum laude). My work sits where models meet infrastructure: I take AI from a notebook to a platform that processes thousands of documents a day, is observable, reproducible and safe to change.

At **AXA Italy** I design and build a distributed document-intelligence platform: FastAPI microservices orchestrated with Durable Functions that **classify, extract, summarize and reconcile** insurance documents, a **RAG layer on Elasticsearch**, and the Terraform, CI/CD, Datadog and Databricks/MLflow stack that keeps it running.
Before that I worked on quant data infrastructure at **Intesa Sanpaolo**, AWS ML pipelines at **Data Reply**, and time-series anomaly detection research with **Cisco**.

items: GCP (Cloud Storage, Dataproc, BigQuery, Vertex AI)

bullets: Designed and built a **distributed document-intelligence platform** processing **10,000+ documents**: Durable Functions orchestration fanning out work across FastAPI microservices.
Developed GenAI services to **classify, extract, summarize and reconcile** policy and claim documents, with Pydantic-validated structured outputs and confidence-based human review.
Built the **RAG layer on Elasticsearch** (BM25 + dense vectors, metadata filters, grounded answers with citations) for complex policy analysis.
Owned the platform around it: **Terraform** IaC, **Jenkins & GitHub Actions** CI/CD, **Docker** images, **Datadog** observability and **Databricks + MLflow** for experiments and evaluation.

Joined in-house from Data Reply to continue the **250TB+** banking data migration to GCP, owning the **data-ingestion software**: a configurable PySpark engine supporting multiple load strategies (**SCD Type 2**, snapshot, incremental/append and more).

Automated ingestion setup: table configurations written in **Excel or plain natural language** are turned automatically into validated **JSON configuration files**, replacing slow, error-prone manual work.
Built a **clustering-based model** that fingerprints Spark workloads and picks the optimal **Dataproc** configuration for each job, improving cluster resilience and cost efficiency.
Optimized Spark transformations through **vectorization** (Pandas UDFs / Arrow): **25% shorter** processing time.
Stack: GCP (Cloud Storage, Dataproc, BigQuery, Vertex AI), PySpark, Bitbucket CI.
Automated inference pipelines for refund-request classification on SageMaker and Spark, delivered with Terraform and Jenkins CI/CD.
Designed event-driven architectures with AWS Lambda and Step Functions for reliable, auditable workflows.

As a consultant for **Intesa Sanpaolo**, started the **250TB+** banking data migration (Teradata / Hadoop → GCP) and the ingestion engine behind it, then joined the client in-house to carry it forward.
Built a multivariate anomaly-detection system reaching a **90% detection rate** with controlled false negatives; presented to Cisco R&D.
Developed a change-detection algorithm for high-frequency telecom streams, handling non-stationarity with Statsmodels and TensorFlow.

caseStudy.label: Case study · AXA Italy
caseStudy.title: A distributed *document-intelligence* platform
caseStudy.intro: Insurance runs on documents: policies, claims, contracts, attachments. This platform turns **10,000+ unstructured documents** into data that is classified, structured, summarized, cross-checked and searchable. I designed the architecture and built the core services, the orchestration and the retrieval layer, then took it to production with infrastructure-as-code, automated delivery and end-to-end observability.

caseStudy.pipelineTitle: How a document flows through the system

pipeline.title: Ingest
pipeline.desc: Documents land in storage and get a tracked job. Ingestion is idempotent, so a document can be reprocessed safely without duplicates.

pipeline.title: Orchestrate
pipeline.desc: A Durable Functions orchestrator fans out one workflow per document, checkpoints state, retries failed steps and fans results back in. Thousands of documents run in parallel without losing progress.

pipeline.title: Parse & chunk
pipeline.desc: Text and layout extraction, layout-aware chunking and metadata enrichment (type, business line, dates) to prepare content for both the AI services and retrieval.

pipeline.title: Classify · Extract · Summarize
pipeline.desc: Each step is a FastAPI microservice called by the orchestrator. Outputs are validated against Pydantic schemas before moving on.

pipeline.title: Reconcile
pipeline.desc: Extracted fields are matched across related documents and against reference data. Mismatches become explicit, auditable findings.

pipeline.title: Index & answer
pipeline.desc: Chunks and embeddings are indexed in Elasticsearch; the RAG API answers questions grounded in the sources, with citations.

services.name: Classification
services.desc: Assigns document type and business line so each document follows the right path.

services.name: Extraction
services.desc: Schema-driven extraction of the fields that matter: policy numbers, parties, dates, coverages, amounts.
details: Field-level provenance back to the source

services.name: Summarization
services.desc: Concise summaries of long documents for operators and downstream processes.

services.name: Reconciliation
services.desc: Cross-checks what was extracted across documents and source systems to surface inconsistencies.

rag: **Hybrid retrieval**: BM25 for exact terms (policy codes, clause names) combined with dense kNN vectors for meaning, with fused ranking.
**Metadata filters** (document type, business line, date) to scope every query to the right subset of the corpus.
**Chunking tuned for long policy documents** and context-window optimization, so the model sees the relevant clauses and nothing more.
**Grounded answers with citations**, evaluated on curated question sets tracked in MLflow.

platform.desc: Stateless containerized microservices, coordinated by durable orchestrations with retries and checkpointing.
Large-scale data preparation on Databricks; MLflow for experiment tracking, model and prompt versioning and evaluation runs.
Distributed traces across services, structured logs, dashboards on throughput, latency and errors, and alerting.
Every environment is reproducible from code: services, search cluster, storage, networking and monitoring.
Lint, type-check and tests on every change; image build and promotion through environments.
Typed contracts between every component, tests on the critical paths, and structured logging everywhere.

github.name: Rag-multi-provider
github.title: High-precision RAG for 100k+ similar documents
github.desc: A retrieval pipeline built for the hardest case: very long, near-duplicate documents. It deduplicates, chunks hierarchically, searches two ways and reranks before the LLM sees anything.
highlights: 3-level hierarchical chunking (2048 / 512 / 128 tokens) with parent walk-up
Dense (bge-large on Qdrant) + BM25, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, cross-encoder reranking
Pluggable LLM providers (OpenAI or local Ollama)
